close_reason: Investigated; not a real bug. The handle_metadata_set handler only invokes create_object::<Metadata>, and the trait invariant documents that backends must support Metadata::TYPE_NAME. Future-bug concern (O != Metadata bypassing uniqueness) belongs in P1 maintainer-burden, filed separately.
description:
Trigger: an O::SetObject that serialize-then-deserializes round-trips to a Metadata variant where required-fields are missing. In memory.rs:702-708, if O::TYPE_NAME==Metadata::TYPE_NAME but serde_json::from_value::<Metadata>(val.clone()) fails, the function returns SetError(InvalidProperties). But the value 'val' has not yet had the server-assigned id injected, and the function proceeds to inject the id and call O::deserialize at line 729. Wait — re-reading: lines 702-722 are early returns. If they pass, line 724 mints the id. So this is fine on re-read.

Re-reading more carefully: in line 696-697, val is created from serde_json::to_value(&obj) where obj is O (caller's generic type). For O = Metadata, val is the wire shape. Lines 703-721 attempt to convert val to Metadata for uniqueness checking. If this succeeds, key is computed and conflict checked.

Edge case I missed: O does not have to be Metadata. The handler passes Metadata, but the trait is generic and the doc invariant requires the backend to support O::TYPE_NAME == Metadata::TYPE_NAME. If a future caller passes O != Metadata, lines 702-722 skip the uniqueness check entirely. supports_type<O> in the trait is the gatekeeper. The handler does not consult supports_type before calling create_object. Not a bug in current scope but a future-bug magnet.

Downgrading. Closing — not a real correctness defect today; the current handler only ever passes Metadata.
title: MemoryBackend.create_object loses uniqueness check when typed-deserialize fails after JSON round-trip
